brief.subject: CFPB targets debanking at large banks
brief.headline: CFPB Launches Initiative on Debanking by Large Banks
brief.dek: The CFPB is acting on large-bank debanking flagged by the OCC, and new application data shows secured-card approval rates by credit score.
brief.lede: The CFPB says it is taking its next step against large banks that cut off customers, building on debanking findings from the OCC.

sections.heading: CFPB moves on bank debanking
bullets: The CFPB announced a new initiative on October 14 aimed at debanking by large banks.
The effort follows up on debanking cases that the OCC, a federal bank regulator, uncovered.
Debanking means closing or denying accounts, which can disrupt how households get paid and pay bills.
The bureau frames the move as part of President Trump's push against debanking tied to constitutionally protected rights.

sections.heading: Secured card odds by score
bullets: New application data breaks down secured credit card approval rates by credit score band.
Secured cards require a deposit and are a common way to build or rebuild credit.
Knowing approval odds by score can help you avoid applications likely to be denied.

brief.seo_description: The CFPB launches a new initiative on large-bank debanking flagged by the OCC, plus secured credit card approval data by credit score.
